Traupman 313
Traupman 367

celer, celeris, celere

adjective, third declension; comparative celerior, superlative celerrimus

fast, quick, swift

The general word for speed, of people, animals, ships and thoughts, the opposite of tardus; celeriter, quickly (see quickly), celeritās, speed (see speed).

Other words

  • vēlōx, vēlōcis — fleet, swift (of running and flying)

    adjective, third declension, one ending · also used · classical · Plin. NH 9.20: vēlōcissimum omnium animālium; Phaedr. 4.2.10–11: mūrēs vēlōcēs

    Of speed of movement, in animals and runners above all: the dolphin, the hare, the hound.

  • rapidus, rapida, rapidum — rushing, rapid

    also used · classical · Lewis & Short: of waters, winds and fire

    (chiefly poetic in this sense (Verg., Ov.))

    First tearing, seizing (of fire and heat); then rushing along, of rivers, winds and horses. Not the everyday word for a fast person (that is celer).

Examples

  • vēlōcissimum omnium animālium, nōn sōlum marīnōrum, est delphīnus

    the fastest of all animals, not only of the sea, is the dolphinPlin. NH 9.20

  • cum vēnātōrem celerī pede fugeret lepus

    when a hare was running from a hunter on swift feetPhaedr. App. 28.1

See also quickly, speed, hurry up!, slowly.
